scope.summary: Implement the measurement solver per Section 13.17 (BK-17.4, TAI-BK-054), closing SREQ-009 and OBR implication 6: numeric targets in centimetres (bust_circ_cm, waist_circ_cm, hip_circ_cm, shoulder_width_cm, penis_length_cm, ...) solved to channel values WITHIN the target's own region group without touching channels of any other region; solve results are ordinary channel edits (events, CRDT, validation), and unreachable targets return a typed nearest-achievable result, never a silent clamp.
acceptance_criteria: solve_measurements(body_id, targets: BTreeMap<String, f64 cm>) resolves each named target to the channels of its owning region group only; the returned SolveResult lists per-target: solved channel edits, achieved value, and status Achieved | NearestAchievable { achieved_cm } | UnknownTarget.

Measurement extraction reuses the tailor-solver extractor lane (13.7 §7.1 measurement rows) against the evaluated body mesh; solver iterates channel values (bounded iterations, documented tolerance) until the extracted measurement meets the target within tolerance.
Region isolation proof: solving bust_circ_cm changes only 'breast' group channels — a post-solve assertion shows all other groups' channel values bit-identical.
Targets beyond designed range return NearestAchievable with the closest achievable value (design_max clamp is reported, not silent).
Applied solves emit ordinary TailorBodyChannelChanged events per edited channel (solver produces no privileged write path).
scope.risk_if_missed: Numeric targeting is the LLM-workflow contract ('make bust Y cm') — without region-isolated solving, a measurement request perturbs unrelated regions and silently violates the decoupling law, making model-driven batch body generation untrustworthy.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
